You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def solve(inp):
    a=np.array(inp); H,W=a.shape
    # candidate lines: rows/cols where a run of repeated non-bg dominates? Use: rows that are ~uniform except isolated dots
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(a.flatten()); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # a line row: pattern of repeated runs of equal colors (vertical stripes) - detect via variance of consecutive runs
    def line_score(arr):
        vals=[arr[i] for i in range(len(arr))]
        # count color changes
        ch=sum(1 for i in range(len(vals)-1) if vals[i]!=vals[i+1])
        return ch
    # horizontal lines: rows with many identical runs -> low change count relative to W? no, lines alternate colors.
    # better: rows where >80% of cells belong to exactly one non-bg color family? demo1 rows: 3s dominate with 2s etc.
    # heuristic: a row is a line if it is composed of long runs (run lengths >=3)
    def runs(arr):
        n=0;last=None;rl=[]
        for x in arr:
            if x==last: n+=1
            else: rl.append(n);n=1;last=x
            if x!=last: rl.append(n);n=1;last=x
        return rl
    rl_rows=[]
    for r in range(H):
        rs=runs(a[r]); ok=max(rs)>=3 and len(rs)>1 and sum(1 for x in rs if x>=3)>len(rs)*0.6
        if ok: rl_rows.append(r)
    cl_cols=[]
    for c in range(W):
        rs=runs(a[:,c]); ok=max(rs)>=3 and len(rs)>1 and sum(1 at [x for x in rs if x>=3])>len(rs)*0.6
        if ok: cl_cols.append(c)
    return bg,rl_rows,cl_cols

    # line color = second most common (the stripe color), markers = rare colors

    v=[c for c in range(W) if all(a[r][c]!=bg or a[r][c] in marc or a[r][c] in linecolor for r in range(H))]
    I=[[int(a[r][c]) for c in v] for r in h]
    out=[]
    for i in range(len(h)-1):
        rr=[]
        for j in range(len(v)-1):
            cs={I[i][j],I[i+1][j],I[i][j+1],I[i+1][j+1]}
            rr.append(int(cs.pop()) if len(cs)==1 and cs!={bg} else bg)
        out.append(rr)
    return out

import numpy as np, json
from collections import Counter
def solve(inp):
    a=np.array(inp); H,W=a.shape
    cnt=Counter(a.flatten()); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    marc=set(c for c,n in cnt.items() if n<=H*W*0.05)
    h={r for r in range(H) if any(a[r][c] in marc for c in range(W))}
    v={c for c in range(W) if any(a[r][c] in marc for r in range(H))}
    I=[[int(a[r][c]) for c in sorted(v)] for r in sorted(h)]
    out=[]
    for i in range(len(h)-1):
        rr=[]
        for j in range(len(v)-1):
            cs={I[i][j],I[i+1][j],I[i][j+1],I[i+1][j+1]}
            rr.append(int(cs.pop()) if len(cs)==1 and cs!={bg} else int(bg))
        out.append(rr)
    return out
ti=G['Test input']
p=solve(ti)
print(json.dumps(p))
# diffs vs previous submissions
prev1=[[3,3,3,3],[3,3,3,3],[3,3,3,9]]
print('vs prev:',[ (i,j,p[i][j],prev1[i][j]) for i in range(3) for j in range(4) if p[i][j]!=prev1[i][j]])

import numpy as np, json
from collections import Counter

def solve(inp):
    a=np.array(inp); H,W=a.shape
    cnt=Counter(a.flatten()); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # line color = most common non-bg; markers = rare
    lcolor=cnt.most_common(2)[1][0]
    marc=set(c for c,n in cnt.items() if c!=bg and c!=lcolor)
    h={r for r in range(H) if any(a[r][c] in marc for c in range(W))}
    v={c for c in range(W) if any(a[r][c] in marc for r in range(H))}
    I=[[int(a[r][c]) for c in sorted(v)] for r in sorted(h)]
    out=[]
    for i in range(len(h)-1):
        rr=[]
        for j in range(len(v)-1):
            cs=[I[i][j],I[i+1][j],I[i][j+1],I[i+1][j+1]]
            s=set(cs)
            if len(s)==1 and next(iter(s)) in marc:
                rr.append(next(iter(s)))
            else:
                mc=max((n for n,x in Counter(cs).items() if x in marc), default=None)
                rr.append(mc if mc is not None else bg)
        out.append(rr)
    return out

for k in ['Demo pair 1 input','Demo pair 2 input','Demo pair 3 input']:
    p=solve(G[k]); o=G[k.replace('input','output')]
    print(k,'match' if p==o else 'NO',p)
print(json.dumps(solve(G['Test input'])))
